subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class TUI cross-channel observe or mirror mode, and should that mode be read-only, interactive, or kept outside core?
rationale: The request intentionally crosses session and channel visibility boundaries and may add public CLI/config surface, so automation cannot safely choose the product scope or authorization model.

options.title: Read-only observer mode
options.body: Add an explicit TUI observer mode that can view authorized same-agent activity without sending replies or changing delivery routes.

options.title: Interactive mirror mode
options.body: Allow bidirectional visible mirroring across surfaces, accepting higher message-delivery and privacy complexity for power users.

options.title: No core mode
options.body: Keep OpenClaw core session-scoped and route broad cross-channel forwarding or mirroring to plugin or ClawHub implementations.

recommendation.title: Read-only observer mode
recommendation.body: Add an explicit TUI observer mode that can view authorized same-agent activity without sending replies or changing delivery routes.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current routing candidate from the related TUI live-update work and security/product context.
